jobs.title: Sr. Workforce Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Sr. Workforce Intelligence Analyst

Business Intelligence and AI-Enabled Self-Service

About The Role

McKesson's Workforce Intelligence team transforms workforce data into clear, trusted insights that help leaders make better decisions. We combine high-quality business intelligence, thoughtful analysis, and practical technology enablement to make workforce information easier to access, understand, and use.

As a Senior Workforce Intelligence Analyst, you will design and deliver visualization, reporting solutions, data products, and decision-ready insights across key workforce topics. You will translate business needs into intuitive analytical experiences, connect and model data, define meaningful metrics, and help stakeholders confidently interpret and act on workforce information.

You will use approved AI capabilities to improve the speed, quality, and accessibility of BI work, and you will help build agentic and conversational solutions that enable responsible self-service for defined Workforce Intelligence use cases. When advanced data science is appropriate, you will partner with data science, technology, privacy, legal, and governance teams.

Key Responsibilities

Business Intelligence and Reporting

Design, develop, and maintain intuitive dashboards, reports, scorecards, and data products using Power BI or similar business intelligence platforms.
Translate business questions into clear analytical requirements, data models, measures, visualizations, and user experiences.
Build scalable, reusable reporting solutions that balance enterprise consistency with the needs of specific stakeholder groups.
Analyze workforce data to identify meaningful trends, patterns, relationships, and opportunities across topics such as workforce composition, talent movement, retention, recruiting, engagement, and organizational health.
Develop concise narratives and recommendations that connect analytical findings to business decisions and actions.
Continuously improve reporting solutions based on user feedback, adoption, changing priorities, and evolving business needs.

Data Preparation, Modeling, and Quality

Combine and transform data from multiple HR and business sources into reliable datasets for analysis and reporting.
Develop and maintain semantic models, calculations, metric definitions, and reporting logic that support consistent interpretation of workforce information.
Write and optimize SQL queries and use appropriate data preparation tools to support reporting and analysis.
Validate data, investigate discrepancies, document business rules, and partner with data owners to resolve quality issues.
Apply data governance, privacy, security, and access requirements throughout the design and delivery of workforce intelligence products.
Maintain clear documentation for data sources, definitions, transformations, assumptions, and known limitations.

AI-Enabled Productivity and Self-Service

Use approved AI assistants to support activities such as requirements synthesis, code development, documentation, quality checks, insight summarization, and content refinement, with appropriate human review.
Design and help build agentic, conversational, or natural-language solutions that enable users to access and navigate approved Workforce Intelligence content and use cases through self-service.
Ground AI-enabled experiences in governed data, approved metrics, curated knowledge, role-based access, and clear business rules.
Partner with product, data, technology, security, privacy, legal, and governance teams to test and operationalize AI-enabled self-service solutions responsibly.
Evaluate AI-enabled experiences for usefulness, accuracy, transparency, adoption, and appropriate escalation to human experts.
Help users understand the appropriate application and limitations of AI-supported insights. Advanced modeling and machine learning development will be completed in partnership with specialized teams when needed.

Stakeholder Partnership and Insight Delivery

Partner with Workforce Intelligence consultants, HR partners, and business stakeholders to clarify needs, frame business questions, and prioritize analytical work.
Facilitate discovery sessions, define success criteria, and convert broad requests into practical BI solutions.
Present complex information in a clear, concise, and actionable manner for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Enable stakeholders to use dashboards and self-service tools effectively through demonstrations, documentation, and targeted education.
Build trusted relationships by setting clear expectations, communicating tradeoffs, and delivering high-quality work.

Continuous Improvement and Team Contribution

Stay current on business intelligence, data visualization, analytics engineering, and responsible AI practices relevant to Workforce Intelligence.
Identify opportunities to simplify recurring work, automate manual processes, improve user experience, and increase adoption of existing products.
Contribute to standards and reusable practices for dashboard design, metric development, documentation, quality assurance, and AI-enabled self-service.
Provide guidance and peer support to analysts and contribute to a collaborative, curious, and delivery-focused team culture.
Support proofs of concept for new BI and agentic capabilities, with an emphasis on practical value, responsible use, and sustainable ownership.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Information Systems, Mathematics, Human Resources, Business, or a related field. Equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
Minimum of 7 years of experience in business intelligence, reporting, data analysis, analytics engineering, or a related role.
Experience developing analytical products for HR, Workforce Intelligence, people analytics, or another business function with complex and sensitive data is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience partnering with business stakeholders to translate needs into adopted reporting or self-service solutions.

Required Technical And Analytical Skills

Advanced proficiency in Power BI or a comparable BI platform, including dashboard development, data modeling, calculations, visualization, and publishing.
Strong SQL skills and experience preparing, joining, transforming, and validating data from multiple sources.
Experience designing semantic models, reusable measures, governed datasets, and scalable reporting solutions.
Strong understanding of data visualization, user-centered dashboard design, analytical storytelling, and self-service BI principles.
Ability to analyze complex data, distinguish signal from noise, identify limitations, and develop clear, evidence-based insights.
Working knowledge of data quality, metadata, governance, privacy, security, and role-based access practices.
Comfort using approved AI tools to support productivity and analytical workflows, with sound judgment and human validation.

Workforce Intelligence and Business Skills

Understanding of workforce metrics, HR data, talent processes, and the decisions supported by workforce intelligence.
Ability to frame ambiguous business questions, define useful measures, and recommend an appropriate analytical approach.
Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including the ability to explain data and technology concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Strong collaboration, consulting, prioritization, and project management skills.
High attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and commitment to reliable, responsible, and decision-useful analytics.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or comparable analytics and data preparation tools.
Experience with HR systems and data sources such as Workday, employee listening platforms, or recruiting systems.
Experience designing or supporting conversational analytics, AI agents, natural-language query, retrieval-augmented generation, or other governed self-service experiences.
Working knowledge of Python or R for data preparation, automation, or exploratory analysis.
Experience supporting product adoption, user enablement, or analytics product management.

Role Emphasis

This role is best suited for an experienced BI professional who can turn complex workforce data into trusted, intuitive, and actionable analytical products. Success will be measured by the quality, usability, adoption, and business value of the solutions delivered, including responsible AI-enabled self-service, rather than by the volume of machine learning models developed.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Senior Data Analyst – Strategic & Program Analytics

Location:
Dallas, TX | Hybrid or Remote
Compensation:
$100–140k Base Salary

A mission-driven organization in Dallas is looking for Senior Data Analysts
to join a growing Strategic Analytics function focused on using data to tackle some of the city's most complex social challenges.

This organization works at the intersection of data, public policy, healthcare, housing, education, criminal justice, and community programs
, partnering with public agencies and community organizations to turn evidence into action. The broader mission is ambitious and measurable: helping dramatically reduce child poverty across Dallas by improving how public resources and programs reach children and families.

These are not traditional reporting or dashboard-focused analyst positions. We're looking for people who can take broad, ambiguous real-world questions
, determine what can legitimately be answered with the available data, conduct rigorous analysis, and translate their findings into recommendations that leaders can actually act on.

The Opportunities

There are multiple openings across two types of Senior Data Analyst roles:

Senior Data Analyst – Strategy

You'll operate as a cross-functional analytical problem solver, working on questions that may come directly from city officials, agency leaders, foundations, and internal leadership.

One week you might be investigating where eligible families aren't accessing public benefits; another could involve understanding geographic gaps in healthcare access, patterns in school attendance, housing affordability, or public safety.

This role leans heavily into statistics, public and administrative data, and analytical judgment
. You'll need to understand not only how to perform an analysis, but whether the available data can actually support the conclusion someone wants to draw. The underlying JD specifically emphasizes regression, sampling and weighting, hypothesis testing, missing data, and understanding the limitations of estimates.

Senior Data Analyst – Program

You'll embed with a specific program area such as housing, maternal health, public safety, benefits delivery, or criminal justice
, becoming that team's dedicated analytics partner.

You'll learn the program's strategy, stakeholders, and recurring decisions, then use data to help the team understand what's happening, why it matters, and where resources or interventions may have the greatest impact.

Both roles involve working heavily with messy, real-world datasets
, with much of the information coming from publicly available sources and administrative data rather than perfectly structured internal systems.

What You'll Do:

Turn ambiguous stakeholder requests into clearly defined, answerable analytical questions.
Source, combine, clean, and analyze public, administrative, and internal datasets.
Evaluate data quality, missingness, sampling issues, outliers, margins of error, and other limitations before drawing conclusions.
Apply statistical methods such as regression, hypothesis testing, sampling, and weighting
where appropriate.
Identify confounding factors and clearly communicate what the data does and does not
support.
Build clean, reproducible analytical workflows using R, Python, Stata, or similar tools
.
Translate complex findings into concise recommendations, decision memos, and visuals for non-technical stakeholders.
Partner directly with program leaders, public agencies, and community stakeholders to influence resource allocation, program design, and strategy.
Use AI-assisted tools across research, coding, and QA while independently validating the methodology and final conclusions.

What We're Looking For:

3–4+ years of applied analytical experience
solving real-world business, policy, research, healthcare, consulting, or program-related problems.
Strong statistical foundations and the judgment to determine which analytical approach is appropriate — and when the data isn't strong enough to support a conclusion.
Hands-on experience working with messy, complex datasets
, ideally including public, administrative, healthcare, policy, demographic, or other real-world data.
Fluency in at least one analytical programming language such as R, Python, or Stata
.
Experience creating reproducible, well-documented analytical workflows.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly translating technical analysis for non-technical decision-makers.
A consultative mindset: you're comfortable receiving an unclear question, figuring out what the stakeholder actually needs to know, and independently determining how to answer it.

Nice to Have:

Experience in one or more of the following would be particularly valuable:
Program evaluation / impact evaluation • causal inference • quasi-experimental methods • health outcomes or HEOR • economic or quantitative consulting • public policy analytics • geographic/spatial analysis • demographic analysis • government or nonprofit analytics

Benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, retirement savings with employer match, generous PTO and holidays, and professional development support.

Medica is a nonprofit health plan with more than a million members that serves communities in Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Missouri, and beyond. We deliver personalized health care experiences and partner closely with providers to ensure members are genuinely cared for.

We're a team that owns our work with accountability, makes data-driven decisions, embraces continuous learning, and celebrates collaboration — because success is a team sport. The Healthcare Data Analyst performs intermediate-level analytical work to evaluate medical, financial, and operational data and support organizational decision-making. This role applies established analytical techniques to identify trends, assess performance, and produce reliable reports and insights. Operating with developing autonomy, the analyst interprets results, explains findings to partners, and resolves moderately complex analytical questions. The position contributes to team objectives by delivering accurate analyses, strengthening reporting consistency, and supporting improvement initiatives across healthcare programs. Perform Analytical Studies & Foundational Modeling
Conduct quantitative analyses and basic modeling to assess medical cost, utilization, and operational performance
Apply established statistical methods and tools under defined guidelines
Interpret results, identify key drivers, and validate outputs for accuracy
Summarize findings in clear, structured formats for review and discussion

Support Metrics, Reporting, & Analytical Frameworks
Prepare and maintain standard reports, dashboards, and monitoring tools
Apply defined data requirements and metric definitions consistently
Perform data validation and reconciliation to ensure reporting integrity
Recommend incremental improvements to reports or analytic processes

Evaluate claims, utilization, pharmacy, or operational data to identify patterns
Compare actual experience to expectations and explain variances
Quantify preliminary financial or operational impacts of observed trends
Develop charts and summaries that highlight actionable insights

Support cross-functional projects through data preparation and analysis
Explain methodologies and results with growing confidence and independence
Document assumptions, methods, and limitations for transparency

Share observations that support process or reporting enhancements
Continue developing technical and healthcare domain expertise

Our London office is based just a stone’s throw from the magnificent St. Paul’s Cathedral on bustling King Edward Street. Here you’ll find modern workspaces and a state-of-the-art auditorium space. Collaborate with colleagues across the research group including our equity analyst peers to deliver innovative cross-asset insights
You will work closely with our internal partners in Sales and Trading to optimise our service to our investing client base.

What We Are Looking For

Proven ability to produce written research that meets the firm’s standards for the basis of recommendations and risk management.
Previous experience covering corporate credit or corporates, regardless of asset class is highly preferred.

jobs.description:
National Operations Manager

THE OPPORTUNITY:

A leading nationwide security organization
is seeking an experienced National Security Operations Manager
to oversee and drive operational performance across a portfolio of a major national account.

This is a senior-level opportunity for a proven security and operations leader who has experience managing large, complex, multi-site security programs
and working with enterprise-level clients and senior executives.

The ideal candidate will come from a large national security company, major security services organization, or the corporate security function of a Fortune 500 or similarly large organization
. This individual will bring a strong understanding of security operations, client management, workforce management, performance metrics, and the complexities of delivering consistent service across a national footprint.

The organization is experiencing continued growth and is looking for a leader who can help strengthen operational execution, expand client relationships, drive accountability, and build scalable processes across the business.

THE ROLE:

The National Security Operations Manager
will provide strategic and operational leadership for major national security accounts, serving as a senior partner to both clients and internal leadership.
This individual will oversee account performance across multiple markets and locations, working closely with field operations, regional leadership, corporate functions, and client executives to ensure consistent service delivery and achievement of business objectives.
The successful candidate will be comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels
— developing national account strategies while also understanding the operational details required to execute successfully across a large geographic footprint.
The role requires a highly accountable, data-driven leader with demonstrated experience managing large-scale security operations, national accounts, or enterprise security programs
.

IDEAL BACKGROUND:

We are particularly interested in candidates who have held senior account or operations leadership positions with:
Large national security companies or security services organizations
National or global security providers
Large contract security organizations
Fortune 500 or similarly sized companies with substantial corporate security operations

Organizations managing large, multi-site security programs
Companies with significant geographically dispersed workforces and operations

Relevant backgrounds may include National Account Manager, National Operations Manager, Regional Vice President, Regional Operations Director, Director of Operations, Corporate Security Leader, or similar senior-level roles.

QUALIFICATIONS:

8+ years of progressive experience
in security, account management, operations, corporate security, or a closely related field.
Demonstrated experience managing large national or multi-site security programs/accounts
, preferably across multiple states or regions.
Experience working for a large security services organization, national security provider, or Fortune 500/corporate security organization
strongly preferred.
Proven experience managing complex client relationships and working directly with C-suite executives, senior leadership, and other key decision-makers
.
Strong understanding of security operations, workforce management, client service delivery, compliance, and operational performance
.
Demonstrated ability to lead through multiple layers of management and influence operational leaders across a geographically dispersed organization.
Strong financial and business acumen, including experience with budgets, forecasting, labor costs, profitability, KPIs, and account performance
.
Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making skills.
Demonstrated success identifying operational challenges, developing solutions, and implementing scalable processes and best practices.
Excellent executive communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.
Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities across a national footprint.
Ability to travel nationally as required.

KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY:

National Operations & Account Oversight

Provide strategic oversight of operational performance across assigned national accounts.
Ensure consistent execution of security services, policies, procedures, and client requirements across multiple markets.
Monitor key operational, financial, staffing, and service-level metrics to identify trends and performance gaps.
Partner with regional and field leadership to resolve operational challenges and drive continuous improvement.
Establish and implement national best practices designed to improve service quality, efficiency, consistency, and client satisfaction.
Ensure account operations remain aligned with contractual requirements and client expectations.

Leadership & Organizational Development

Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to a geographically dispersed team of operational leaders.
Partner with regional and local management to establish clear performance expectations and accountability.
Develop and mentor operational leaders to strengthen the organization's leadership pipeline.
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer service, and operational excellence.
Drive consistency in the execution of policies, procedures, and operational standards across the national footprint.

Strategic Planning & Business Performance

Develop and execute strategic operating plans for national accounts.
Analyze account performance, financial results, staffing levels, client feedback, and other business metrics to identify opportunities for improvement.
Partner with executive leadership on growth strategies, account expansion, retention, and operational scalability
.
Develop action plans to address underperforming locations, accounts, or operational areas.
Identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce costs, increase efficiency, and strengthen overall account profitability.
Support organizational growth initiatives and new business opportunities as appropriate.

Client & Executive Relationship Management

Serve as a senior-level point of contact for key national clients.
Establish and maintain trusted relationships with client executives and senior stakeholders.
Understand client business objectives and translate them into effective security and operational strategies.
Lead executive-level business reviews and account meetings.
Present operational performance, financial results, trends, challenges, and strategic recommendations to clients and internal leadership.
Proactively identify opportunities to strengthen client relationships, expand services, and increase overall account value.
Manage escalated client issues and coordinate cross-functional resources to ensure timely resolution.

Performance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and monitor meaningful KPIs across national accounts.
Utilize operational and financial data to identify trends and drive informed decision-making.
Develop corrective action plans and ensure successful implementation.
Benchmark performance across locations and identify opportunities to replicate successful practices.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance service delivery, employee performance, client satisfaction, and financial results.

Career development and advancement opportunities
Opportunity to play a significant leadership role within a growing nationwide security organization

As consumers embrace new AI-driven experiences, the LiveRamp data collaboration network exponentially expands the breadth and accuracy of the data on which marketing AI capabilities operate, powering deeper customer insight and measurable performance on a global scale. LiveRamp is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with offices worldwide. Learn more at LiveRamp.com.

We are looking for a highly-motivated, business-minded Legal and Data Ethics Operations Analyst. This person will help the Data Ethics and Legal teams solve internal problems, implement goal-oriented strategies and play a key role in the Data Ethics team.

This role strengthens operational execution across jurisdictions through process improvement, responsible AI enablement, privacy and legal operations, playbook development, and effective management of data subject requests.

You Will

Coordinate data subject request management, including intake, categorization, routing, deadline tracking, documentation, communications, and closure; work with the Data Ethics team on high-risk, complex, sensitive, or multi-jurisdictional requests.
Build and maintain practical playbooks, decision trees, checklists, templates, escalation criteria, and role-based guidance for recurring data ethics, privacy, legal, and regulatory processes.
Manage privacy questionnaire workflows by coordinating intake, preparing AI-assisted first drafts from approved information, maintaining supporting evidence, and escalating questions requiring legal, privacy, security, or data ethics judgment.
Support the design of responsible AI controls including approved-source use, permissions, confidentiality, traceability, version control, audit trails, quality checks, and human approval before material outputs are used.
Study our organizational workflows and processes to recommend and implement changes to help improve business processes and optimize overall operations.
Participate in creating team functional process documentation, creating presentation materials and facilitating or leading cross functional teams through projects and/or issues.
Co-ordinate, write and maintain information and knowledge resources to ensure it is kept up to date and supports users of the system(s). This includes managing and organizing documents within the Data Ethics department to ensure that they are accurate, up-to-date, and easily accessible.
Create, modify, and manage content on the Data Ethics intranet site.
Assist with the project planning, scheduling, and documentation of various department projects, such as working with subject matter experts to assist with designing and organizing training course content and may use instructional technology tools to develop participant materials, videos, practical exercises, and interactive eLearning.
Prepare operational reporting on questionnaire and request volumes, turnaround times, escalations, recurring issues, automation performance, risks, and improvement opportunities.

Your Team Will

Our Data Ethics operations program is designed to enable LiveRamp to meet its privacy-related legal requirements and reasonable expectations of clients while minimizing and mitigating risk to LiveRamp. Our mission is to help the business find safe and legal ways to use data for the betterment of our products, services and consumers. The team operates as a connected, cross-border function that helps LiveRamp find safe, legal, ethical, and scalable ways to use data while supporting consistent execution across all locations.

About You

Degree in a relevant discipline
Experience in a similar role required with relevant experience in data privacy, data ethics, legal operations, regulatory operations, or related process enablement
Experience completing critical analysis, review and editing of written documents
Ability to work in a collaborative manner to develop strong working relationships with the business and key stakeholders to facilitate data compliance while enabling commercial opportunities and support them in improving data protection and governance practices
Comfortable receiving loose requirements and working with internal team members to identify project objectives, collaborate to further define requirements, pull and validate the data, present the data to the end-users, and make refinements as needed. Strong communication and organizational skills are a must.
Ability to translate complex legal, regulatory, and data ethics requirements into practical processes, playbooks, decision trees, and guidance.
Experience applying AI or automation to privacy questionnaires, document or contract-template updates, knowledge retrieval, playbook creation, triage, or workflow orchestration.
Hands-on experience building, configuring, or implementing AI agents, automation, or AI-assisted workflows in a controlled business environment.
Self-motivated, proactive, and eager to dive into the business, data workflows, and technology
Comfort with ambiguity, multi-tasking, and independence
Excellent written/verbal communication, presentation, drafting and negotiation skills
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to organize, prioritize, manage deadlines, and handle complex escalations in a fast-paced and demanding work environment

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
At Verda, we're building a full-stack AI cloud, covering everything from data centers and hardware to our own cloud platform that the world's leading AI teams use to do serious AI work.

We strive to make a positive mark on the world through the infrastructure we build and give leading teams a service they can truly depend on. Headquartered in Helsinki, we operate globally with offices in London and San Francisco.

Join Verda while it’s still being built - not once it’s finished.

Why Verda

Cash and equity compensation along with local benefits.
40+ nationalities, with 6 different ones on the management team.
A real chance to make an impact and work alongside world class engineers, researchers, and partners across the global AI ecosystem.

The role

We're one of the fastest-growing companies in Europe, and growth at this pace generates a dangerous amount of data: revenue run ramps, GPU utilization, capacity projections, unit economics, sales and marketing funnels, product usage. Every team is asking for numbers, and every number has to actually mean something.

That's where you come in. As our Senior Data Analyst
, you make sense of how the business performs across very different product lines, going deepest on R&D and revenue, and put that understanding in front of the people making the calls. Some of that is analysis. Some of it is improving what the business already runs on: the dashboards and tools behind the numbers, and the unified, reliable reporting you own together with data engineering and GTM systems.

This doesn't start from zero. The warehouse is in use, teams run on existing dashboards, and the rhythm of reviews, goals, and deep dives already depends on analytics. Your job is to advance it to next level: keep the work efficient, set the standards, and build what's still missing as we grow. We are looking for someone who reads that as an opportunity, not a warning.

What you'll do

Leverage large data sets to derive insights that inform business decisions, focusing on the business, product and operational performance across multiple distinct product lines
Gain in-depth knowledge of Verda's business operations, with a special focus on R&D and revenue strategies.
Communicate effectively with business leaders to influence strategic decision-making, presenting complex data in a consumable format.
Collaborate with cross-functional global teams, contributing to strategic initiatives with data insights and strategic recommendations.
Conceptualize, develop, and maintain centralized tools and dashboards for data extraction and business management.
Collaborate and build together with data engineering and GTM systems teams to integrate diverse data sources, ensuring the creation and maintenance of reliable, unified reports
Set the analytics operating standards across the company: documentation, data-quality checks, review practices, and how analytics work gets prioritized.
Support analytical rhythms of the business through regular reviews, goal setting, and deep dives.

What we're looking for

5+ years in analytics & data analysis, including ownership of company-level metrics or KPI systems.
Strong skills in both qualitative and quantitative analysis, including content analysis, hypothesis testing, cluster analysis, and statistical techniques.
Fluency with BI tooling (Looker, Metabase, Tableau, or equivalent) and with telling a decision-ready narrative instead of just shipping charts.
Working Python skills for analysis and automation, comfortable in notebooks, scripts, and version control.
Business understanding across cloud products, finance, sales, and marketing.
Excellent communication skills, capable of presenting technical content to non-technical audiences.
Proven ability to initiate and complete analytical projects independently.
Action-oriented with a natural curiosity for detail and a strong analytical mindset.

Nice to have

Experience in usage-based pricing businesses: utilization, capacity, and margin analysis
Hands-on dbt or a semantic-layer / metrics-store setup
Experience building AI-assisted analytics workflows from 0 to 1
People-leadership ambitions

Practicalities

Location: London, UK
Work arrangement: hybrid, 3 days per week in our office
Employment type: Full-time and permanent

What's Next

We're building fast and this role needs the right person behind it. There's no artificial deadline, but when we find who we're looking for, we move. If this sounds like your next move, apply now.

Please submit your application through our Careers page. We don't accept applications sent by email.

The Operations Analyst supports the operational and financial performance of Physicians East by analyzing data, monitoring departmental performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting organizational initiatives.

Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including provider productivity, appointment utilization, patient volumes, staffing efficiency, and departmental performance.

Identify operational trends, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.

Departmental revenue, expenses, and financial performance.

Patient satisfaction and operational quality measures.

Evaluate staffing levels, overtime, and labor productivity relative to operational needs.

Support financial modeling, business planning, and feasibility assessments for new or expanded services.

Collaborate with finance and revenue cycle teams to identify opportunities to improve financial performance.

Process Improvement and Operational Support

Evaluate existing workflows and recommend improvements to increase efficiency and consistency.

Assist department managers in identifying and resolving operational challenges.

Support the implementation of standardized processes, policies, and procedures.

Participate in initiatives involving patient access, scheduling, staffing, and departmental performance.

Monitor the effectiveness of operational improvements and report outcomes to leadership.

Data Management and Analysis

Extract, validate, and analyze information from electronic health records, practice management systems, and other organizational platforms.

Develop recurring reports and dashboards for executive leadership and department managers.

Ensure operational data is accurate, consistent, and delivered timely.

Translate complex data into clear findings and practical recommendations.

Identify data integrity issues and coordinate resolution with appropriate departments.

Project and Strategic Initiative Support

Assist leadership with planning, implementing, and monitoring operational projects.

Track project milestones, deliverables, and performance outcomes.

Conduct research and benchmarking to support operational decisions.

Prepare executive summaries, presentations, and recommendations for leadership review.

Support organizational growth initiatives, service expansion, and operational restructuring.

Minimum Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Finance, Analytics, or related field required.

Master's degree preferred.

Experience

Minimum of three years of experience in healthcare operations, business analytics, financial analysis, or a related field.

Experience in a multi-specialty physician practice, medical group, or large healthcare organization preferred.

Experience developing operational dashboards, performance scorecards, and management reports preferred.

Familiarity with electronic health records and practice management systems required; NextGen experience preferred.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, formulas, and data analysis.

Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting tools preferred.

Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and confidentiality.

Key Performance Expectations

Accuracy and timely completion of monthly departmental scorecards.

Development and maintenance of standardized operational dashboards.

Identification of measurable opportunities for operational improvement.

Effectiveness in supporting departmental productivity and efficiency initiatives.

Acquisitions and feasibility
Assist in identifying and assessing new development opportunities, including consented sites, airspace, conversions and redevelopment.
Carry out technical and commercial feasibility studies: planning history, density, unit mix and design options to maximise development potential.
Prepare preliminary development appraisals (GDV, residual land value and viability) using sales and rental comparables.
Assess Section 106, CIL and affordable housing obligations and their impact on viability.

Planning
Review planning records, planning policy (London Plan, local plans, Greater Manchester policy) and planning risks.
Develop planning strategies, including full planning applications and Section 96A and Section 73 routes for scheme revisions and uplift.
Coordinate planning applications with consultants and local planning authorities.

Contractor procurement and cost management
Identify, prequalify and engage main contractors, specialist subcontractors (including rooftop and LGSF specialists) and consultants such as QS, PM, EA, MEP and structural engineers.
Issue drawings and tender information packs, obtain budget pricing and run tender comparisons.

Advise on procurement routes: Design and Build, Construction Management, traditional, PCSA and ECI.

Construction delivery

Review progress, quality and programme with contractors and consultants.
Report to senior management on project status, risks and costs.

Degree in architecture, civil or structural engineering, construction management, real estate or a related built-environment discipline.

AutoCAD or Revit.
Full UK driving licence.

jobs.description:
Role Description We are seeking analytical, detail-oriented, and commercially minded professionals for the positions of Trade Finance Specialist / Trade Operations Analyst. These roles focus on supporting international trade transactions, managing trade finance documentation, coordinating banking operations, and ensuring that trade-related activities are processed accurately and efficiently. Successful candidates will contribute to transaction management, operational risk control, documentation verification, and compliance with established banking procedures.
Trade Finance Specialists are responsible for supporting trade finance products and services, including letters of credit, documentary collections, bank guarantees, and other trade-related financial instruments. Key duties include reviewing trade documents, checking transaction details against applicable requirements, coordinating with clients and financial institutions, and supporting the issuance or processing of trade finance instruments. They also assist with transaction structuring, document discrepancy resolution, customer inquiries, and the preparation of trade finance records. Collaboration with relationship managers, compliance teams, and international banking partners helps ensure that transactions meet contractual, operational, and regulatory requirements.
Trade Operations Analysts focus on monitoring and processing trade-related transactions, reviewing supporting documents, reconciling records, and analyzing operational performance. Responsibilities include validating transaction information, tracking payment and settlement activities, investigating processing discrepancies, maintaining accurate databases, and preparing operational reports. They help identify potential delays, documentation errors, and process inefficiencies while coordinating with internal departments and external counterparties to resolve issues. As a Talent Transformation Program Manager, you will be the single point of accountability for enablement inside a small number of strategic enterprise customers that have made a significant investment in Databricks training.

Think of the role as the training equivalent of an account executive. Once a customer invests in training, you make sure they use what they bought, see the value, and come back for more. You'll own each customer's enablement program end to end: the learning plan, the operating cadence, use of their training investment, the insights gathered along the way, and the next training opportunity.

You'll work alongside the Databricks account team (account executives, solutions architects and professional services) and coordinate our instructors, curriculum, certification and training operations teams to deliver.

Responsibilities

Drive customer engagement

Run the operating cadence with the customer and the account team: weekly check-ins, monthly reviews and quarterly business reviews
Identify and build a relationship with an executive training sponsor at the customer early in the engagement
Share clear, regular status updates covering progress, what's next, and any risks, each with a recommended solution

Own the learning plan and its delivery

Turn each customer's training investment into a structured, time-bound learning plan by role and skill level, tied to the customer's business priorities and use cases
Track what's been purchased, used and scheduled, and make sure training is used on time rather than left to expire
Secure delivery capacity (instructors, dates, lab environments, travel) ahead of time against the plan

Capture technical context

Run discovery deep enough to understand what the customer's teams are building, which tools they use, and where their skill gaps are
Produce hand-off summaries that a solutions architect or instructor can act on without another meeting

Turn training into customer insight

Make sure the account team receives a summary after every training session covering attendance, use cases, blockers, new teams and suggested next steps
Share important signals with the account team quickly, along with a recommended next step

Grow the partnership

Work with the account team to map the customer's use cases and proactively recommend where training would speed adoption or reduce support issues
Identify and drive training expansion and renewal opportunities through to close, backed by a clear training proposal
Get involved before new training agreements are signed to confirm scope, formats, lab needs, travel and success measures, so there are no surprises later

8+ years in program management, customer success, account management or training, with a track record of high-touch engagements with enterprise customers

1+ years in data, analytics, AI or cloud

Proven ability to own a portfolio of customers, drive outcomes across many teams, and move forward without waiting for direction

Strong commercial instincts: able to spot opportunities and take them to close with an account team

Technical enough to run credible discovery on a modern data and AI platform (data engineering, SQL and BI, streaming, data governance, machine learning and generative AI). You're not expected to deliver hands-on training.

Executive presence with customer learning leaders and business sponsors; comfortable leading kickoffs and business reviews

Data-driven: you report with numbers (learners, utilization, enrollments, satisfaction, pipeline), not anecdotes

Fast, clear communicator: same-day follow-ups, no surprises, and a solution with every problem

Comfortable with ambiguity and building a new program from the ground up

Experience in a training, enablement or learning business, in either sales or delivery

new_jobs.title: Project Manager HCI
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members.

Project Description

The Heart of Conservation Initiative
( HCI
) is a 5-year
global project
designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas.  

Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. 

This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation; and (v) monitoring and evaluation.

Job Description

LOCATION: This position will be based in Brazil, Kenya, or Cambodia.

Major Function

The Project Manager will lead the GCU’s support for the HCI partners and ensure successful delivery of all components. They will supervise staff in a Global Coordination Unit (GCU), provide day-to-day management of the project and, with support from the Partner Liaison, coordinate with ten (10)  Component 1 Partners, and partners and specialists in Components 2 through 5.  This is a unique role managing and representing a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous Peoples and local community partners’ priorities as well as meet GEF requirements. 

The Project Manager will report to the Senior Director, Conservation Areas, and Senior Director, Inclusive Conservation (Project Co-Leads)

Key Responsibilities

 Technical Delivery of Project Components:  
Component 1: Work with Component 1 partners to review and approve their annual work plans and budgets, provide technical inputs to their on-the-ground work, as needed, and support their self-strengthening plans.    
Component 2: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 2 with GCU staff support; Work with Component 1 partners to identify common capacity-strengthening needs and develop and implement a collective strengthening program.  
Component 3: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 3 with GCU staff support; Design and implement the Youth Policy Leaders program and work with Component 1 and 2 partners to identify policy processes and to enable effective, HCI-supported engagement therein.  
Support GCU staff to ensure successful delivery of Components 4 and 5.
 Project Management: 
Day-to-day management, monitoring, and evaluation of project activities and results as outlined in the CERDoc, Grant Agreement, and Annual Work Plan and Budget to achieve the project objective and targets in the Results Framework. 

Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:  

Ensure that the GCU holds regular virtual meetings with Component 1 (C1) partners and as required with additional partners involved in the other components,  
Manage the workflow for the Indigenous Global Steering Committee (IGSC), in collaboration with the Project Co-Leads. 
In collaboration with all project sub-grantees and partners, develop the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) for the global HCI for each project year, for no-objection from the WWF GEF Agency and approval by the IGSC.  
Share C1 Partners’ annual workplans and budgets for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency and for IGSC information.  Provide high-level oversight and monitoring of procurement and expenditure in line with the AWPB in collaboration with the Finance and Operations (FO) Manager.
Review progress of work plan and monitoring plan in collaboration with the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer.  
Responsible for organization of inception workshop and other critical project workshops and meetings. 
Manage the design and maintenance of a project website, and the development and implementation of a communications strategy in collaboration with the Communications and Knowledge Management (CKM) Officer. 
Provide support for project implementation support and learning visits and internal and external reviews/evaluations with relevant GCU staff.
Support the MEL Officer to organize annual reflection workshops to identify lessons learned and propose potential changes for adaptive management to ensure project results and indicator targets are reached. 
Troubleshoot with GCU staff, component partners and Project co-leads to address challenges and create enabling conditions for trusting partnerships and project success.
Maintain a project risk register, including identification of risks to project success and development of mitigation measures in coordination with C1 partners and other project partners.  
Prepare and execute a project exit plan, including hand-off of project equipment and resources, close of grants and agreements, consultations and communications with project partners and interested parties, and ensure sustainability of project results. 
Champion the promise and achievements of the project, elevating its contributions to systems change and Indigenous Peoples and local community-led partners whenever possible. 
Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment.
Staff management: 
Supervise the GCU staff including MEL Officer (crosscutting, especially components 1, 4 and 5), FO Manager (crosscutting), Environmental and Social Safeguards Officer (crosscutting, especially component 1), Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Officer (crosscutting , especially component 1), CKM Officer (crosscutting, especially components 2 and 4), Logistics and Administrative Assistant (crosscutting), and any other directly recruited staff or consultants.
Prepare TORs to recruit consultants, staff and sub-contracts in consultation with Project Co-Leads and for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency. 
Reporting: 
Collaborate with the MEL Officer to aggregate information from Component 1 Partner sub-projects and formulate semi-annual Project Progress Reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Prepare workshop reports following the inception and other critical project workshops.
Collaborate with the FO Manager to oversee the preparation and disbursement of sub-grants to Component 1 partners and grants and agreements under the other 4 components.  
Collaborate with the FO Manager to aggregate financial information from C1 Partners and oversee the development of quarterly financial reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Collaborate with the WWF network and partners to ensure co-finance reporting on a yearly basis. 
Prepare a Project Close Report.  
Quality Assurance: 
Provide quality assurance for project activities, including sub-grants. 
Provide quality assurance through review of reports and other products from partners, technical specialists, consultants, and staff.
Ensure implementation in line with the GEF and WWF standards and policies. 
Week-long, international travel may be expected on approximately a quarterly basis. 
Partnerships: 
Coordinate with co-financed projects and liaise with project partners to ensure co-financing commitments are realized.  
Attract additional partners and co-financing. 
Ensure smooth coordination and communication among all project partners, and with the Component 1 partners (the latter in collaboration with Partner Liaison). 
Manage stakeholder engagement and ensure gender and social inclusion considerations are fully integrated throughout project implementation in collaboration with the Social and Environmental Safeguards (ESS) and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Officers.  
Represent the project at conferences, meetings, and workshops. 

Qualifications

Key Competencies

Strategic Collaboration and Leadership. Able to lead and influence large and highly dispersed teams and coalitions, dealing with risk mitigation and conflict management.
Intercultural and adaptive management skills 
Results-oriented project management
Collaboration
Cross-cultural communication

Skills And Abilities

10 years of technical working experience, including at least five years of project management experience.  
Bachelor’s Degree; post-graduate degree in a relevant field preferred. 
At least five years’ experience supporting and working in solidarity with Indigenous people and local community organizations, and a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
Demonstrated ability to interact with Indigenous peoples and local community representatives, senior government, NGO, business, and donor staff. 
Experience with the Convention on Biological Diversity and/or other multilateral agreements and processes, focusing on biodiversity, Indigenous peoples’ and local communities’ rights, and finance. 
Experience delivering technical and financial reporting to donor agencies on large projects. 
Experience managing similar, complex, multi-stakeholder and multi-country projects.
Experience leading a team of staff and coordinating sub-grant partners, ideally across multiple time zones and cultures.  
Technical experience and knowledge in the thematic area of the project, such as Indigenous -led territorial stewardship, community-based sustainable development, etc.   
Knowledge of the Open Standards for the Practice of Conservation, or WWF Project and Program Management Standards, preferred. 
Experience with GEF Projects and GEF knowledge an advantage. 
Written and spoken fluency in English required; advanced proficiency in Spanish, French, or Portuguese – highly preferred.   

Additional Information

Location

The position will be based in Brazil, Cambodia or Kenya.

If applying to work in Brazil or Kenya, applicants must be nationals legally authorized to work in Brazil or Kenya. Employment visa sponsorship and relocation are not provided for Brazil or Kenya.

PLEASE NOTE: If applying to work in Cambodia, nationals from South and Southeast Asian countries who are willing to relocate to Cambodia may also apply, and WWF-Cambodia may be able to support visa sponsorship and relocation costs based on available budget.

Please note:
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the job's location.
Position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship.

new_jobs.title: Information Technology Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
RBox International Solutions, Inc. is a Philippines-based organization providing business and operational support services. We are currently hiring for an IT Program Manager or Senior IT Project Manager
to support enterprise technology initiatives and collaborate with U.S.-based stakeholders.

Work Arrangement:
Full-time | Permanent Night Shift (9:00 PM–6:00 AM PHT) | Work From Home

Position Overview

The Senior Program Manager
leads a portfolio of concurrent technology projects across software engineering, ERP, CRM, system integration, and compliance. This role translates business priorities into delivery plans, manages dependencies across teams and vendors, and reports progress and risks directly to executive leadership.
The Senior Program Manager sets delivery standards for the team, coaches Technical Project Managers, strengthens PMO practices, and helps establish a developing PMO. This is a fully remote position reporting to U.S.-based IT leadership, with a fixed night shift aligned with U.S. business hours.
Responsibilities
Portfolio Delivery:
Lead multiple concurrent technology projects, manage cross-team dependencies, and deliver committed outcomes on time and within scope.
Planning and Estimation:
Ensure documented project plans are established in Azure DevOps (ADO) before development begins. Review estimates, balance team capacity, and recommend project sequencing when priorities compete.
Executive Reporting:
Prepare weekly executive status reports and quarterly business reviews. Provide evidence-based RAG ratings, highlight business impact, and identify decisions requiring leadership attention.
Intake and Scope Control:
Manage incoming requests and changing priorities. Evaluate tradeoffs, implement change control, and communicate recommendations with clear alternatives.
Risk and Escalation:
Proactively identify portfolio risks, escalate concerns with actionable recommendations, and drive timely resolution.
Vendor and Partner Management:
Oversee delivery vendors and implementation partners, including statements of work (SOWs), milestones, acceptance criteria, and performance management.
Requirements and Solution Alignment:
Collaborate with business owners, business systems analysts, and engineering teams to define business requirements, align solutions, and establish acceptance and launch criteria.
Delivery Metrics:
Define and monitor delivery KPIs using ADO data, including on-time delivery, scope changes, carryover, and cycle time.
Regulated Delivery:
Incorporate regulatory and compliance requirements, including SOC 2 and applicable industry standards, into project plans, change control, documentation, and audit processes.
Coaching and PMO Standards:
Mentor Technical Project Managers in planning, ADO practices, and reporting. Improve PMO templates, intake processes, and performance metrics.
Automation and AI:
Drive automation initiatives for recurring PMO activities, including AI-assisted status reporting and dashboards.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
At least 6 years of project management experience in IT, software, or technology, including 3 years managing multiple concurrent projects or cross-functional programs.
Demonstrated experience delivering enterprise technology projects, including ERP, CRM, or system integrations.
Advanced proficiency in Azure DevOps or Jira, including portfolio backlogs, queries, and dashboards.
Experience presenting project updates, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership.
Experience managing vendors, SOWs, milestones, and project acceptance.
Experience coaching or mentoring project managers.
Hands-on experience in project planning, execution, monitoring, and reporting.
Willingness to work a fixed night shift, 9:00 PM to 6:00 AM Philippine Time, with at least 12 months of continuous prior night shift experience.
Reliable home internet connection of at least 25 Mbps, backup internet, and a dedicated private workspace.

Preferred Qualifications

PMP or PgMP certification, along with PSM or SAFe certification.
Experience delivering ERP, CRM, EDI, or data platform programs.
Experience working in regulated industries, including pharmaceutical distribution, or with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 and DSCSA.
Experience developing Power BI dashboards using ADO data.
Experience establishing or improving PMO practices, including project intake, templates, governance, and KPIs.
Familiarity with AI-assisted tools for project management, reporting, and automation.

Why Join Us?

Help shape and strengthen a developing Project Management Office.
Collaborate directly with U.S.-based IT leadership and gain exposure to executive stakeholders.
Manage a diverse portfolio of enterprise technology, integration, and compliance initiatives.
Explore professional growth opportunities toward PMO leadership.
Work with modern project management, analytics, and AI-assisted reporting tools.
Enjoy a fully remote work arrangement.

is actively looking for a Transformation Program Manager
for an AI-enabled software delivery transformation focused on applying AI to software delivery practices. This role is 100% remote but candidates must be able to work CST!

***This is a 12 month contract with the opportunity to extend based on performance and business needs***

This initiative will use a phased pilot-team approach
to evaluate how AI can improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and create measurable cost savings. This Program Manager will work with business, technology, engineering, offshore teams, vendors, internal AI leadership, and senior stakeholders to shape and execute the AI-enabled delivery model.
This role requires a hands-on program leader who can operate in ambiguity, create structure where the path is still being defined, drive decisions, remove obstacles, and keep the initiative moving toward measurable outcomes.

Responsibilities

Lead planning and delivery for the AI-enabled software delivery transformation, including workstreams where the process, operating model, or implementation path is still evolving.

Drive day-to-day execution across pilot teams, stakeholders, vendors, and offshore engineering partners.

Build and manage the integrated project plan, including training, pilot execution, testing, adoption, measurement, and reporting.
Clarify ownership, frame options and tradeoffs, drive decisions, and escalate issues when needed.
Track milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, and action items through resolution.
Help turn the AI-enabled delivery approach into practical guidance, documentation, and repeatable ways of working.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager – Networking NPI
new_jobs.description:
About Nscale

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About The Role

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to lead New Product Introduction (NPI) for networking across Nscale's US GPU cloud. You'll own the path from a new network platform, architecture, or vendor being selected to it being proven, documented, and ready to deploy at scale.

That covers new switch and NIC generations, 800G and next-generation optics, new cluster fabric designs, and new data center and WAN reference architectures. You'll work closely with Network Architecture and Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, vendors, and our Deployment organization, which takes what you qualify and builds it across our sites. The role involves some travel to vendor labs and US pilot sites.

What You'll be Doing

Own the NPI program for new networking platforms, from vendor selection and early samples through lab qualification, pilot build, and release to Deployment.
Build NPI plans with clear phase gates (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent), entry and exit criteria, owners, and dates.
Drive qualification and validation of switches, NICs/DPUs, optics, cables, and network operating systems, including interoperability, performance, burn-in, and failure testing.
Run the vendor engagement on new products: roadmap alignment, sample allocation, bug and RMA tracking, firmware and NOS release readiness, and escalation of blocking defects.
Partner with Network Architecture to turn new designs into production-ready reference builds, golden configs, BOMs, cabling and rack standards, and acceptance test plans.
Lead first-of-a-kind pilot builds, capture lessons learned, and feed them back into designs before scale-out.
Own the handoff to Deployment: documentation, training, readiness reviews, and a supply plan that supports the volume ramp.
Track technical, schedule, and supply risks across new product lines; make trade-offs visible and drive decisions with engineering and leadership.
Build the NPI process itself, including templates, gate reviews, dashboards, and reporting, so new platforms land predictably as we grow.

About You

5+ years in technical program management, hardware NPI, or network engineering, with direct ownership of bringing new network hardware or architectures into production.
Experience at a hyperscaler, major network or silicon vendor, or ODM/OEM (e.g. Microsoft, AWS, Meta, Google, Oracle/OCI, NVIDIA, Cisco, Arista, Broadcom), or a comparable large-scale environment.
Hands-on familiarity with hardware qualification: lab validation, interop testing, firmware and NOS lifecycle, defect triage, and phase-gate NPI processes.
Strong technical grounding in data center and cluster networking: Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics, RoCE, BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, optics and transceivers, and structured cabling.
Proven ability to drive vendors and cross-functional engineering teams to decisions when designs, schedules, and supply are still moving.
Comfortable working in ambiguity, defining process where none exists, and making clear calls on readiness.
Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting technical trade-offs to senior leadership.
Willingness to travel to vendor labs and pilot sites as needed.

Nice to Have

NPI experience on networking for large GPU clusters, HPC, or AI training environments.
Experience qualifying 400G/800G/1.6T optics, co-packaged or linear-drive optics, or new SerDes generations.
Familiarity with HPC topologies (Fat Tree, Rail-optimized, Dragonfly) and NVIDIA Spectrum-X or Quantum InfiniBand platforms.
Exposure to network automation and test tooling (Python, Ansible, traffic generators such as IXIA/Keysight or Spirent).
Background in supply chain or manufacturing ramp for new hardware.
PMP, PgMP, or similar certification.

Why this role matters

Every new generation of GPU cluster depends on network hardware that has never run at our scale before. This role makes sure each new platform is proven before it reaches a site, so Deployment can build it fast and right the first time.

new_jobs.description:
ATI has been named "Best Places to Work in SC" from 2017 - 2026.

This is a full-time opportunity with benefits
ATI provides Medical, Dental and Vision Plan options
